title: Bill Lear figuring out gravity control

tellings.quote: In fact, a 1956 article for Jane's Defence Weekly states, "And William Lear, the autopilot wizard, is already figuring out gravity control for the weightless craft to come."

Bill Lear is quoted in 1956, you know, he was the father of John Leer and invented the first, you know, jet. Yeah. Lear Jet, first private jet. basically. And he said, you know, I believe anti-gravity is possible because UFOs display them.
tellings.difference: Has Lear himself saying anti-gravity is possible because UFOs display it, rather than a Jane's article saying he is working on gravity control.
tellings.link_reason: Both describe Bill Lear's 1956 public link to gravity control and anti-gravity.

plain: A podcast host, Jesse Michels, talks about Bill Lear, the inventor behind the Learjet, the first private jet, and father of John Lear. In one telling Michels quotes a 1956 article in Jane's Defence Weekly, a military trade publication, saying Lear was "already figuring out gravity control for the weightless craft to come." In another, Michels says Lear himself said in 1956 that he believed anti-gravity was possible because UFOs display it. Either way, Michels tells it as a sign that serious aviation figures in the 1950s took gravity control seriously.
